important_observations: The 1979 first printed page uses two descriptive and operational A/B/C conventions within one report; earlier comparison relied on an oversimplified two-alphabet model. This is documentary reclassification only, without changing source text.
The 1983 fig.2 is a secondary printed derivative of Holst estimated drawing, not a second independent 17th-century geodetic plan.

Fig.3 offers a 1-meter printed scale bar and north indication for a locally metric gate footprint, but has no projected coordinates, no local control-point table, no excavation-coordinate grid or datum in inspected source.
Solid and hatched zones are visually distinct in Fig.3; absent explicit original/restored legend, neither color nor hatch is automatically phase-certified.

Fig.4 has a stratigraphic frame 1:50, labels I/II/III for walls and 1–8 layers; older and later structure are distinguishable stratigraphically but their world-coordinate original vertex is not supplied.
Photographs 5–13 corroborate excavation wall details and blocked doors, but do not provide a measured repeatable same-object 2026 survey.
Numeric widths 4.15m and 3.70m refer to separate gate complexes; they are not source-to-modern control-point coordinates.
